    @pytest.mark.priority(7)
    @allure.title("validate the newly created event appears with correct details in the dashboard's Upcoming Appointments widget")
    def test_case_7(self):
        self.scheduler.go_to_dashboard()
        self.scheduler.wait_for_visible(SchedulerPage.VIEW_CALENDAR_LINK)
        assert self.page.locator(SchedulerPage.VIEW_CALENDAR_LINK).is_visible()
    
        row_locator = SchedulerPage.appointment_row(self.__class__.event_name)
        self.scheduler.wait_for_visible(row_locator)
        assert self.page.locator(row_locator).is_visible()
    
        detail_text = self.page.locator(SchedulerPage.appointment_detail_line(self.__class__.event_name)).inner_text()
        # The widget renders date, "·", time, "·" and duration as separate
        # lines (e.g. "Aug 4\n·\n3:00 PM\n·\n60m"), then appends the attendee
        # line (e.g. "Nobody yet") after that, all within the same container.
        # Drop the "·" separator lines and take the first three remaining
        # lines as date/time/duration.
        lines = [line.strip() for line in detail_text.splitlines() if line.strip() and line.strip() != "·"]
        actual_date, actual_time, actual_duration = lines[:3]
    
        # e.g. "Jul 30, 2026 · 2:00 PM EDT" -> date "Jul 30", time "2:00 PM"
        # (the widget's time has no timezone suffix, so drop the tz token).
        list_date_part, list_time_part = [part.strip() for part in self.__class__.list_date_time_text.split("·")]
        expected_date = list_date_part.split(",")[0].strip()
        expected_time = " ".join(list_time_part.split()[:2])
        expected_duration = "".join(ch for ch in self.__class__.expected_duration_text if ch.isdigit()) + "m"
    
        assert actual_date == expected_date, f"expected date {expected_date!r}, got {actual_date!r}"
